overview: Write Note and OutboxMutation atomically to IndexedDB before acknowledging saved locally. A foreground sync coordinator retries stable mutation IDs, uses expectedVersion and stores remote tombstones. Service worker caches the versioned app shell, not arbitrary private API responses; background sync is optional enhancement. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.calculation: ~10 MB raw text plus indexes, outbox and copies
estimation.result: Budget quota overhead; expose export and sync status rather than promise unlimited durability
estimation.implication: Test denied storage, quota exhaustion, schema upgrade and a browser restart during sync.

components.purpose: Write Note and OutboxMutation atomically to IndexedDB before acknowledging saved locally. A foreground sync coordinator retries stable mutation IDs, uses expectedVersion and stores remote tombstones. Service worker caches the versioned app shell, not arbitrary private API responses; background sync is optional enhancement. Performance plan: 1,000 notes averaging 10 KB text; offline app shell; browser storage can be evicted and is not a backup guarantee. Accessibility: Keyboard-accessible note list/editor, labelled sync and conflict status, explicit unsaved errors and focus preservation when remote notes arrive. Failure recovery: On 409 keep both versions for merge; never silently overwrite. On transaction failure retain in-memory draft, show unsaved and allow export. A network online flag alone does not prove sync succeeded. Trade-off: Online-first is simpler when offline edits are unnecessary. CRDTs help concurrent rich editing but add substantial complexity for basic notes.

steps.explanation: Validate local input and enter a pending state. Use the component callback rather than mutating server snapshots directly.

steps.title: Send the versioned operation
steps.explanation: Call POST /notes/mutations through the API adapter. Request: {mutationId:"mut1",noteId:"n1",expectedVersion:4,body:"Edited",deleted:false}. A prior successful response or unresolved operation must not be overwritten by a stale retry.

steps.title: Reconcile or expose recovery
steps.explanation: On 409 keep both versions for merge; never silently overwrite. On transaction failure retain in-memory draft, show unsaved and allow export. A network online flag alone does not prove sync succeeded. Update the query key with the acknowledged version or invalidate/refetch it; maintain focus and make pending/error state visible.

failureCases.scenario: Local and remote versions diverge, or storage write fails
failureCases.handling: On 409 keep both versions for merge; never silently overwrite. On transaction failure retain in-memory draft, show unsaved and allow export. A network online flag alone does not prove sync succeeded.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
